prompt.en: A handheld-to-repeater estimate gives only local coverage, but a hilltop weak-signal pair later works many hundreds of kilometres on VHF. What should the log say before claiming an enhanced opening?

text.en: Record antenna heights, weather, distance, direction, and signal steadiness so the range claim can be tied to the path conditions.
Delete the local estimate, because any longer contact proves height and terrain never matter.
Assume the same long path is now dependable for handheld emergency coverage every day.
Log only transmitter power, because lower-atmosphere paths do not depend on weather or antenna location.

explanation.en: The lesson separates ordinary local planning from longer weak-signal paths. Good notes preserve the evidence: station height, weather, direction, distance, and signal character.

prompt.en: A VHF event shifts from brief shower-related pings to a steadier path along a lake inversion. Which operating adjustment best fits the change?

text.en: Schedule long overs for the pings, because short reflections leave more time than inversion paths.
Treat the ping period as short contact windows, then use more normal exchange timing while the inversion path stays steady.
Log both as the same kind of ionospheric opening because the band is VHF.
Ignore timing once the first contact is made; both openings should last the same length.

explanation.en: Meteor-related pings are brief, so timing must be concise. A duct or enhanced lower-atmosphere path can allow more normal exchanges while the weather structure persists, but it still may fade.

prompt.en: During an HF exercise, a control station hears brief smeared bits from a normally missed area, but the traffic is not reliable enough for messages. What is the best operating response?

text.en: Log the clue as possible scattered energy and move traffic to a band, relay, or schedule that gives steadier copy.
Keep sending long messages on that path, because brief smeared copy proves the route is dependable.
Widen the transmitted signal to make all delayed copies arrive with the same phase.
Ignore the band and time in the log, because mixed paths cannot be compared later.

explanation.en: Weak smeared copy can be a useful propagation clue, but it is not a dependable traffic path by itself. The operator should log it and choose a steadier communication plan.
